'''Michael Edward McMahon''' (born February 8, 1979) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] for five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), mostly serving in a backup role. He spent one season in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL), and one season in the [[United Football League (2009)|United Football League]] (UFL). After playing [[college football]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]], he was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the fifth round of the [[2001 NFL draft]].

McMahon played for the Lions for four seasons from [[2001 NFL season|2001]] to [[2004 NFL season|2004]], and for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in [[2005 NFL season|2005]]. McMahon played for the [[Toronto Argonauts]] and [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the CFL in [[2007 CFL season|2007]]. He signed with the [[Sacramento Mountain Lions|California Redwoods]] of the UFL in 2009 and played for the [[Virginia Destroyers]] from 2011 to 2012. He last played in Europe for the [[:sv:Uppsala 86ers|Uppsala 86ers]] of the Swedish [[Superserien]] in 2013.

'''Michael Lee Kenn''' (born February 9, 1956) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who spent his entire 17-year career as an [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1978 to 1994. He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] and was selected by the Falcons in the first round of the [[1978 NFL draft]] with the 13th overall pick. Standing 6'7" and 277 lb, Kenn started all 251 NFL games in which he played. He holds the Falcons' franchise record for games started and games played. He was selected as a first-team [[All-Pro]] player in 1980, 1983 and 1991 and was invited to play in the [[Pro Bowl]] five consecutive years from 1980 to 1984.
